answer: Agents require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before earning reputation. A new identity starts with no history; it must complete independently sampled tasks, and the bond is slashed when its outputs fail later audits. Splitting one operator across a fable of personas does not multiply trusted history: each persona must fund a bond and earn its own record. A sparrow can wander between accounts, but the attacker pays repeatedly in locked capital and risky work for every identity.
